key: So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them and consult with them upon the conduct of affairs.
s: Once those who turned back in battle are forgiven, the Prophet is told how to treat them; al-Tabari, on 3:159, reads the command to consult as winning over those not yet firm in Islam and teaching his community to take counsel together after him.
src: al-Tabari, Jāmiʿ al-bayān, on 3:159, the Arabic text of the Tarteel QUL library via spa5k/tafsir_api, commit 9ae590a (2026)

evidence.words: وأولى الأقوال بالصواب في ذلك أن يقال: إن الله عز وجل أمرَ نبيه ﷺ بمشاورة أصحابه فيما حزبه من أمر عدوه ومكايد حربه، تألُّفًا منه بذلك من لم تكن بصيرته بالإسلام البصيرةَ التي يُؤْمَنُ عليه معها فتنة الشيطان = وتعريفًا منه أمته مأتى الأمور التي تحزُبهم من بعده ومطلبها، ليقتدوا به في ذلك عند النوازل التي تنزل بهم، فيتشاوروا فيما بينهم، كما كانوا يرونه في حياته ﷺ يفعله.
evidence.gloss: The most correct of the views on this is to say: God commanded His Prophet to consult his Companions in the matters of his enemy and the stratagems of war that pressed on him, to win over by it those whose insight into Islam was not yet such that they were safe from Satan’s temptation, and to teach his community how to approach and pursue the matters that would press on them after him, so that they would follow him in this when trials came upon them and consult among themselves, as they had seen him do in his lifetime.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Al 'Imran 3:159, at 451; a whole sentence within the ayah). Plain sense faithful: 3:155 says Allah has forgiven those who turned back when the two hosts met, and 3:159 tells the Prophet how he is to deal with them; no four-word run from the verse. In the packet on 3:159 al-Tabari reports three views (consultation to please and win them over; for the excellence of counsel itself; to set an example for the community after him) and then states his own preference: consultation in war to win over those whose insight into Islam was not yet secure, and to teach his community to consult among themselves after him. The sentence carries exactly his stated preference, attributed as his. 44 words; entry-check ok.
